title: Client Level Segregation of Advisory and Distribution Activities
summary: Ensure client level segregation at IA’s group/family level, where existing clients cannot avail both advisory and distribution services within the same group/family.
trigger: IA's group/family level
required_action: Adopt a compliance and monitoring process for client level segregation.
evidence: Documentation of the adopted compliance and monitoring process, including records of onboarding new clients and existing clients' service eligibility.
source_circular: SEBI/HO/IMD/DF1/CIR/P/2020/182 dated September 23, 2020 and SEBI/HO/MIRSD/MIRSD-PoD-1/P/CIR/2025/003 dated January 08, 2025
verbatim_text: To ensure client level segregation at IA’s group/family level, as per Regulation 22(5) of the IA Regulations, following compliance and monitoring process shall be adopted: (a) Existing clients, who wish to take advisory services, will not be eligible for availing distribution services within the group/family of IA. Similarly, existing clients who wish to take distribution services will not be eligible for availing advisory services within the group/family of IA. (b) A new client will be eligible to avail either advisory or distribution services within the group/family of IA. However, the option to avail either advisory services or distribution services shall be made available to such client at the time of on boarding. (c) Client under these guidelines shall include individual client or non-individual client.

title: Client Level Segregation of Advisory and Distribution Activities - Option for New Clients
summary: Provide new clients with the option to choose between advisory or distribution services at onboarding.
trigger: Onboarding of a new client
required_action: Make available the option to avail either advisory services or distribution services to new clients during onboarding.
evidence: Documentation of the onboarding process, including records of options provided to new clients.
source_circular: SEBI/HO/IMD/DF1/CIR/P/2020/182 dated September 23, 2020 and SEBI/HO/MIRSD/MIRSD-PoD-1/P/CIR/2025/003 dated January 08, 2025
verbatim_text: (b) A new client will be eligible to avail either advisory or distribution services within the group/family of IA. However, the option to avail either advisory services or distribution services shall be made available to such client at the time of on boarding.

title: Client Level Segregation of Advisory and Distribution Activities - Client Discretion
summary: Allow clients discretion in holding assets prior to applicability of segregation.
trigger: Applicability of client level segregation guidelines
required_action: Not force clients to liquidate or switch existing holdings.
evidence: Documentation of client communications regarding their asset holding decisions and any related agreements.
source_circular: SEBI/HO/IMD/DF1/CIR/P/2020/182 dated September 23, 2020 and SEBI/HO/MIRSD/MIRSD-PoD-1/P/CIR/2025/003 dated January 08, 2025
verbatim_text: (d) The client shall have discretion to continue holding assets prior to the applicability of this segregation under the existing advisory/distribution arrangement. However, the client shall not be forced to liquidate/switch such existing holdings.

title: Client Level Segregation of Advisory and Distribution Activities - Permanent Account Number (PAN) as Control Record
summary: Use PAN as the control record for identification and client level segregation.
trigger: Onboarding or existing advisory/distribution services
required_action: Ensure that each client's PAN is used as the control record for identification and client level segregation.
evidence: Client records showing PAN usage for identification and segregation purposes.
source_circular: SEBI/HO/IMD/DF1/CIR/P/2020/182 dated September 23, 2020 and SEBI/HO/MIRSD/MIRSD-PoD-1/P/CIR/2025/003 dated January 08, 2025
verbatim_text: (e) Permanent Account Number (PAN) of each client shall be the control record for identification and client level segregation.

title: Use PAN as control record for client identification and segregation
summary: Investment Advisers (IAs) must use the Permanent Account Number (PAN) of each client as the control record for identification and client level segregation.
trigger: For all clients, regardless of type
required_action: Use PAN as the control record for client identification and segregation
evidence: Client records with PAN details
verbatim_text: Permanent Account Number (PAN) of each client shall be the control record for identification and client level segregation.

title: Jointly and severally use PAN of all members in a family as control record for individual clients
summary: For individual clients, the PAN of all members in their family would jointly and severally be the control record.
trigger: For individual clients with multiple family members seeking investment advisory services
required_action: Use joint and several PANs as the control record for client identification and segregation
evidence: Client records with PAN details of all family members
verbatim_text: In case of an individual client, “family of client” shall be reckoned as a single client and PAN of all members in “family of client” would jointly and severally be the control record. However, the same is not applicable for non-individual clients.

title: Provide annual declaration or periodic update on dependent family members
summary: Clients must provide an annual declaration or periodic update as necessary regarding their dependent family members.
trigger: For clients with dependent family members seeking investment advisory services
required_action: Provide annual declarations or periodic updates on dependent family members
evidence: Client declaration forms or update records
verbatim_text: The dependent family members shall be those members whose assets on which investment advisory is sought/provided, originate from income of a single entity i.e. earning individual client in the family. The client shall provide an annual declaration or periodic updation as the case maybe in respect of such dependent family members.

title: Advise direct plans (non-commission based) only
summary: Investment Advisers must advise direct plans that are non-commission based.
trigger: For all investment advisory services provided
required_action: Advise only direct plans (non-commission based) to clients
evidence: Client records of advised products and services
verbatim_text: The IAs shall maintain on record an annual certificate from an auditor confirming compliance with the client level segregation requirements as specified in Regulation 22 of the IA Regulations. Such annual certificate shall be obtained within 6 months of the end of the financial year and form part of compliance audit, in terms of Regulation 19(3) of the IA Regulations.

title: Maintain annual auditor certificate for client level segregation
summary: Investment Advisers must maintain an annual auditor certificate confirming compliance with client level segregation requirements.
trigger: At the end of each financial year
required_action: Obtain and maintain an annual auditor certificate for client level segregation
evidence: Auditor's certificate confirming compliance with client level segregation requirements
verbatim_text: The IAs shall maintain on record an annual certificate from an auditor confirming compliance with the client level segregation requirements as specified in Regulation 22 of the IA Regulations. Such annual certificate shall be obtained within 6 months of the end of the financial year and form part of compliance audit, in terms of Regulation 19(3) of the IA Regulations.

title: Provide investment advisory services exclusively to institutional clients or accredited investors with a waiver
summary: Investment Advisers providing services exclusively to institutional clients and accredited investors may not be subject to client level segregation requirements if they obtain a standard waiver.
trigger: When providing investment advisory services exclusively to institutional clients or accredited investors
required_action: Obtain and maintain a standard waiver from the client/investor
evidence: Waiver signed by the client/investor
verbatim_text: The IAs providing investment advisory services exclusively to institutional clients and accredited investors may not be subject to compliance with the requirements of segregation of investment advisory and distribution activities provided that the client/investor signs a standard waiver stating the above.

title: Do not consider stock broking activity as distribution activity for client level segregation
summary: Stock broking activity is not considered as distribution activity for the purpose of client level segregation.
trigger: For all investment advisory services provided
required_action: Do not consider stock broking activity as part of distribution activities for client level segregation purposes
evidence: Client records and service agreements
verbatim_text: Stock broking activity is not considered as distribution activity for the purpose of regulation 22 of IA Regulations.

title: Enter into investment advisory agreement with clients
summary: Investment Advisers must enter into an investment advisory agreement with their clients.
trigger: For all new and existing client relationships
required_action: Enter into a written investment advisory agreement with each client
evidence: Signed investment advisory agreements
verbatim_text: Regulation 19(1)(d) of the IA Regulations provides that IA shall enter into an investment advisory agreement with its clients. The said agreement shall mandatorily cover the terms and conditions provided in Annexure A and Most Important Terms and conditions (MITC), as standardized by Industry Standard Forum in consultation with IAASB and SEBI, provided in Annexure B.

title: Include MITC terms and conditions in investment advisory agreement
summary: Investment Advisers must include the MITC terms and conditions in their investment advisory agreements.
trigger: For all new and existing client relationships
required_action: Include MITC terms and conditions in each investment advisory agreement
evidence: Signed investment advisory agreements with MITC included
verbatim_text: MITC must include the following as terms and conditions:: “This agreement is for the investment advisory services provided by the IA and IA cannot execute/ carry out any trade (purchase/ sell transaction) on behalf of the client without his/her specific and positive consent on every trade. Thus, you are advised not to permit IA to execute any trade on your behalf without your explicit consent.”

title: Disclose MITC terms and conditions to clients
summary: Investment Advisers must disclose the MITC terms and conditions to their clients.
trigger: For all new and existing client relationships
required_action: Disclose MITC terms and conditions to each client and obtain consent
evidence: Signed investment advisory agreements with MITC included
verbatim_text: IA shall incorporate the MITC into the investment advisory agreement and shall disclose and take consent from clients on the agreement.

title: Obtain client consent to investment advisory agreement through legally acceptable modes
summary: Investment Advisers must obtain client consent to their investment advisory agreements through legally acceptable modes, including digital signatures.
trigger: For all new and existing client relationships
required_action: Obtain client consent to the agreement via a legally acceptable mode of signature
evidence: Signed investment advisory agreements with valid client signatures
verbatim_text: Consent of client to agreement between IA and client may be signed by the client in person or through any other legally acceptable mode including DigiLocker enabled Aadhaar based e-signature facility.

title: IA must provide guidance on Centralised Fee Collection Mechanism for IA and RA (CeFCoM)
summary: Provide clients with information about the CeFCoM option.
trigger: When entering into an agreement with a client
required_action: Guide the client on the CeFCoM option.
evidence: Client acknowledgment of receiving guidance on CeFCoM.
verbatim_text: IAs shall also provide guidance to their clients in the agreement on the optional ‘Centralised Fee Collection Mechanism for IA and RA’ (CeFCoM).

title: IA can include additional terms and conditions in the agreement without diluting existing provisions
summary: Include additional terms and conditions as long as they do not conflict with existing regulations.
trigger: When entering into an agreement with a client
required_action: Ensure that any additional terms and conditions are compliant with IA Regulations and SEBI circulars.
evidence: Copy of the signed agreement including all additional terms and conditions.
verbatim_text: IA can include additional terms and conditions in the agreement without diluting the provisions of the IA Regulations and amendments thereto as well as circulars issued thereunder.

title: IA must ensure that no investment advice is rendered or fee charged until client signs the agreement
summary: Do not provide services or charge fees before the client has signed and received a copy of the agreement.
trigger: When entering into an agreement with a client
required_action: Ensure that investment advice is not provided nor fee charged until after the client signs the agreement and receives a copy.
evidence: Signed agreement from the client and proof of delivery to the client.
verbatim_text: IA shall ensure that neither any investment advice is rendered nor any fee is charged until the client has signed the aforesaid agreement and provided copy of signed agreement to the client.

title: IA must charge fees in accordance with SEBI regulations
summary: Charge fees as per SEBI guidelines.
trigger: When charging fees from a client
required_action: Charge fees according to the specified modes and limits.
evidence: Proof of fee collection and supporting documents.
verbatim_text: Regulation 15A of the IA Regulations provides that IAs shall be entitled to charge fees from a client in the manner as specified by SEBI. Accordingly, IAs can charge fees under two modes, namely, (i) Assets under Advice (‘AUA’) mode, which is subject to a limit of 2.5 per cent of AUA per annum per family of client across all services offered by IA, and (ii) Fixed fee mode, which is subject to a specified fee limit (earlier limit ₹1,25,000) per annum per family of client across all services offered by IA.

title: IA must not exceed the revised fixed fee mode limit
summary: Ensure that fees charged under the fixed fee mode do not exceed ₹1,51,000 per annum.
trigger: When charging fees from a client using the fixed fee mode
required_action: Do not charge more than ₹1,51,000 per annum under the fixed fee mode.
evidence: Proof of fee collection and supporting documents.
verbatim_text: The maximum fee that may be charged by the IA under the fixed fee mode now stands revised and shall not exceed ₹1,51,000 per annum per family of client. The fee limit shall be revised and announced by IAASB once in three years based on the Cost Inflation Index (CII) after due consultation with SEBI.

title: IA must provide evidence of AUA for fee calculation
summary: Provide supporting documents to demonstrate Assets under Advice.
trigger: When charging fees from a client
required_action: Submit supporting documents like demat statements, unit statements etc. to prove AUA.
evidence: Supporting documents such as demat statements and unit statements.
verbatim_text: The fee limits do not include statutory charges. IA shall be required to demonstrate AUA with supporting documents like demat statements, unit statements etc. of the client.

title: Disclose and seek consent for distributor consideration
summary: Investment Advisers (IAs) must disclose and obtain client consent regarding the additional costs towards distributor consideration when charging fees under AUA mode.
trigger: For clients seeking second opinion on assets under pre-existing distribution arrangement with other entity
required_action: Disclose and seek annual client consent for the additional costs towards distributor consideration.
evidence: Client acknowledgment of disclosure document.
verbatim_text: IAs shall, on annual basis, disclose and seek consent from such clients that apart from the advisory fees payable to the IA, the clients will be incurring costs towards distributor consideration for such assets.

title: Charge fee only on SEBI-regulated securities under AUA mode
summary: Investment Advisers (IAs) can charge fees based on the aggregate net asset value of SEBI-regulated securities.
trigger: For charging fee under AUA mode
required_action: Charge fees only for investment advice related to SEBI-regulated securities.
evidence: Fee calculation records based on SEBI-regulated securities.
verbatim_text: In terms of revised scope of the ‘investment advice’ under Regulation 2(1)(l) of the IA Regulations, Investment advice related to securities under purview of SEBI shall only fall under the purview of IA Regulations. As provided under Regulation 2(1) (ac) of IA Regulations, for the purpose of charging fee under AUA mode, AUA shall mean the aggregate net asset value of securities under the purview of SEBI.

title: Charge fees on pre-existing distribution arrangement assets under AUA mode
summary: Investment Advisers (IAs) can charge a fee not exceeding 2.5% of the value per annum for assets under pre-existing distribution arrangements.
trigger: For clients seeking second opinion on assets under pre-existing distribution arrangement with other entity
required_action: Charge fees not exceeding 2.5% of the value per annum for such assets.
evidence: Fee calculation records based on AUA mode.
verbatim_text: For clients seeking second opinion on assets under pre-existing distribution arrangement with other entity, IAs may charge fee on the assets under pre-existing distribution arrangement under AUA mode, subject to a limit of 2.5% of such assets value per annum.

title: Refund fees for unexpired period on premature termination
summary: Investment Advisers (IAs) must refund the fees for the unexpired period in case of premature termination of IA services.
trigger: Premature termination of IA services as per agreement
required_action: Refund the fees for the unexpired period to the client.
evidence: Client refund records.
verbatim_text: In the event of pre-mature termination of the IA services in terms of agreement, the client shall be refunded the fees for unexpired period. However, IA may retain a maximum breakage fee of not greater than one-quarter fee.

title: Retain breakage fee on premature termination
summary: Investment Advisers (IAs) can retain a maximum breakage fee of not greater than one-quarter of the fees for unexpired period in case of premature termination.
trigger: Premature termination of IA services as per agreement
required_action: Retain a maximum breakage fee of not greater than one-quarter of the fees for unexpired period.
evidence: Breakage fee calculation records.
verbatim_text: In the event of pre-mature termination of the IA services in terms of agreement, the client shall be refunded the fees for unexpired period. However, IA may retain a maximum breakage fee of not greater than one-quarter fee.

title: Charge fees based on specific provisions for individual and HUF clients
summary: Investment Advisers (IAs) must charge fees according to the specified terms and conditions applicable only to individual and Hindu Undivided Family (HUF) clients who are not accredited investors.
trigger: For charging fee under AUA mode for non-accredited individual and HUF clients
required_action: Charge fees based on the specified terms and conditions applicable to such clients.
evidence: Fee calculation records specific to individual and HUF clients.
verbatim_text: The fee related provisions such as fee limit, modes of payment of fees, refund of fees, advance fee, breakage fees shall only be applicable in case of individual and Hindu Undivided Family (HUF) clients (provided these clients are not accredited investors) of IAs. These provisions shall not be applicable in case of non-individual clients and accredited investors.

title: Charge fees based on negotiated terms for accredited clients
summary: Investment Advisers (IAs) must charge fees according to the bilaterally negotiated contractual terms applicable to non-individual and accredited clients.
trigger: For charging fee under AUA mode for non-individual and accredited clients
required_action: Charge fees based on the bilaterally negotiated contractual terms.
evidence: Bilateral contract records.
verbatim_text: The fee related provisions such as fee limit, modes of payment of fees, refund of fees, advance fee, breakage fees shall only be applicable in case of individual and Hindu Undivided Family (HUF) clients (provided these clients are not accredited investors) of IAs. These provisions shall not be applicable in case of non-individual clients and accredited investors.

title: Maintain deposit as per SEBI regulations
summary: Investment Advisers (IAs) must maintain a deposit with the specified amount based on the number of clients.
trigger: On an ongoing basis
required_action: Maintain a deposit in the form of units of liquid mutual fund or overnight mutual fund, or as a deposit maintained with a scheduled bank, marked as lien in favour of IAASB.
evidence: Deposit maintenance records and lien documentation.
verbatim_text: As per Regulation 8 of the IA Regulations, an investment adviser shall maintain a deposit of such sum, as specified by the Board from time to time. In this regard, it is specified that an IA shall maintain the deposit in the form of units of liquid mutual fund or an overnight mutual fund or as a deposit maintained with a scheduled bank. Such deposit shall be marked as lien in favour of IAASB.

title: Deposit Requirement for Clients
summary: Investment Advisers must deposit a certain amount of money as lien in favor of IAASB.
trigger: Number of clients exceeds specified thresholds
required_action: Deposit the required amount of money as lien in favor of IAASB
evidence: Bank statement or other financial records showing the deposit
verbatim_text: The deposit shall be marked as lien in favor of Investment Adviser Administration and Supervisory body (IAASB), in the manner and form as may be specified by IAASB.

title: Revision of Deposit Amount
summary: Deposit amount can be revised based on changes in applicable deposit amounts.
trigger: Change in the maximum number of clients in the previous financial year
required_action: Revise the deposit amount as per the new applicable amount
evidence: Updated records or documents showing the revised deposit amount
verbatim_text: The deposit amount may be revised for any change in applicable amount of deposit, based on the maximum number of clients on any day in the previous financial year, latest by 30th April of the subsequent financial year.

title: Implementation of Deposit Provisions
summary: IAASB must implement necessary systems and procedures for deposit provisions.
trigger: N/A
required_action: Put in place necessary systems and procedures, and notify IAs of the same
evidence: Documentation or records showing implementation of systems and procedures
verbatim_text: IAASB shall put in place necessary systems and procedures for implementation of these provisions and bring the same to the notice of IAs.

title: Review of Qualification and Certification Requirements
summary: SEBI must review qualification and certification requirements from time to time.
trigger: N/A
required_action: Review the qualification and certification requirements
evidence: Documentation or records showing the review process
verbatim_text: The deposit requirements shall be reviewed by SEBI from time to time.

title: Qualification and Certification Requirement for Individual Investment Advisers
summary: Individual investment advisers must meet certain qualification and certification requirements.
trigger: N/A
required_action: Meet the specified qualification and certification requirements
evidence: Documentation or records showing compliance with the required qualifications and certifications
verbatim_text: Vide SEBI (Investment Advisers) (Amendment) Regulations, 2020, enhanced qualification and experience requirement were introduced under Regulation 7 of the IA Regulations for individual investment adviser or a principal officer of a non-individual investment adviser and persons associated with investment advice. Further, in terms of second proviso of regulation 7 (1), it was specified that existing individual IAs above fifty years of age (as on September 30,2020) shall not be required to comply with the enhanced qualification and experience requirements.

title: Relaxed Qualification Requirement for Individual Investment Advisers
summary: Individual investment advisers can meet relaxed qualification and certification requirements.
trigger: N/A
required_action: Meet the specified relaxed qualification and certification requirements
evidence: Documentation or records showing compliance with the required qualifications and certifications
verbatim_text: Subsequently, vide SEBI (Investment Advisers) (Second Amendment) Regulations, 2024, experience requirement was removed and qualification requirement was relaxed under Regulation 7 of the IA Regulations, effective from December 16, 2024. Further, vide SEBI (Investment Advisers) (Second Amendment) Regulations, 2025, the qualification and certification requirement has been further relaxed to inter alia provide that an applicant with graduate degree on any equivalent qualification accompanied with relevant certification from NISM or from any other organization or institution accredited by NISM, shall be eligible to act as Individual investment advisers or principal officer of a non-individual investment adviser and persons associated with investment advice, with effect from November 25, 2025.

title: Further Relaxed Qualification Requirement for Individual Investment Advisers
summary: Individual investment advisers can meet further relaxed qualification and certification requirements.
trigger: N/A
required_action: Meet the specified further relaxed qualification and certification requirements
evidence: Documentation or records showing compliance with the required qualifications and certifications
verbatim_text: Vide SEBI (Investment Advisers) (Second Amendment) Regulations, 2025, as provided under Regulation 7(c), an applicant who has completed Post Graduate Program in the Securities Market (Investment Advisory) from NISM or a Post Graduate Program in Financial Planning from NISM or any other program of NISM as may be specified by the Board shall be eligible to act as Individual investment advisers or principal officer of a non-individual investment adviser and persons associated with investment advice.

title: Obtain Renewal Certification from NISM or an Accredited Institution
summary: Investment Advisers (IAs) must obtain relevant renewal certification from NISM or any other organization accredited by NISM within three years of registration.
trigger: Within 3 years from the date of registration certificate
required_action: Obtain relevant renewal certification
evidence: Renewal Certification Document
verbatim_text: However, as provided under Regulation 7(2), such persons shall be required to obtain relevant renewal certification from NISM or from any other organization or institution accredited by NISM within three years from the date of registration certificate.

title: Intimate Administration and Supervisory Body for Transition to Non-Individual IA
summary: Investment Advisers (IAs) whose number of clients exceeds 300 or fee collected during the financial year exceeds 3 crore rupees, whichever is earlier, must immediately intimate the Administration and Supervisory Body and initiate the process of transition.
trigger: Number of clients exceeds 300 or fee collected during the financial year exceeds 3 crore rupees, whichever is earlier
required_action: Intimate Administration and Supervisory Body and initiate the process of transition from individual IA to non-individual IA within 3 months
evidence: Intimation Letter and Application for In-Principle Approval
verbatim_text: vide SEBI (Investment Advisers) (Second Amendment) Regulations, 2025, Regulation 13(e) of the IA Regulations has been amended to provide that an individual IA, whose number of clients exceeds three hundred at any point of time or the fee collected during the financial year exceeds three crore rupees, whichever is earlier, shall immediately intimate the Administration and Supervisory Body and initiate the process of transition from individual to non-individual investment adviser and apply for grant of in-principle approval for registration as non-individual investment adviser within 3 months from the date on which the threshold is reached.

title: Submit Application for Non-Individual IA Registration
summary: Investment Advisers (IAs) must apply for registration as non-individual IA using FORM-A and provide the requisite fee.
trigger: After initiating the process of transition from individual IA to non-individual IA
required_action: Submit application in FORM-A with the requisite fee
evidence: Application Form and Fee Receipt
verbatim_text: Such application shall be made in FORM-A as per the IA Regulations, along with the requisite fee and same shall be assessed in accordance with the provisions of the IA Regulations and amendments thereto as well as circulars issued thereunder.

title: Complete Transition from Individual to Non-Individual IA within 3 Months
summary: Investment Advisers (IAs) must complete the transition process within 3 months of receiving in-principle approval.
trigger: After receiving in-principle approval for registration as non-individual IA
required_action: Complete the transition from individual IA to non-individual IA within 3 months
evidence: Completion Certificate or Documentation
verbatim_text: The “number of clients” shall mean number of client agreements in force at any point of time i.e. limit of 300 clients not to be exceeded on any day.

title: Surrender Individual IA Registration Certificate upon Completion of Transition
summary: Investment Advisers (IAs) must surrender their individual IA registration certificate after completing the transition process.
trigger: After completing the transition from individual IA to non-individual IA within 3 months
required_action: Surrender individual IA registration certificate
evidence: Surrender Certificate or Documentation
verbatim_text: On completion of transition within the time limit, the IA shall surrender his individual IA registration certificate and will be granted final registration as non-individual IA subject to compliance with all the requisite requirements of registration.

title: Maintain Client Agreement Limit at 300 Clients or Less
summary: Investment Advisers (IAs) must ensure that the number of client agreements in force does not exceed 300 clients on any day during the transition period.
trigger: During the transition period
required_action: Maintain a limit of 300 clients or less at any point in time
evidence: Client Agreement Records
verbatim_text: The “number of clients” shall mean number of client agreements in force at any point of time i.e. limit of 300 clients not to be exceeded on any day.

title: Collect Fees Exceeding Threshold during Transition Period
summary: Investment Advisers (IAs) are permitted to collect fees in excess of the threshold limit during the transition period.
trigger: During the transition period from individual IA to non-individual IA
required_action: Collect fees in excess of 3 crore rupees or 300 clients, whichever is earlier
evidence: Fee Collection Records
verbatim_text: In order to ease the process of transition from individual IA to non-individual IA, an individual IA shall initially be required to apply for grant of in-principle approval for registration as non-individual IA and shall complete the transition from registration as individual investment adviser to non-individual investment adviser by end of three months from the date on which of in-principle approval was granted. On completion of transition within the time limit, the IA shall surrender his individual IA registration certificate and will be granted final registration as non-individual IA subject to compliance with all the requisite requirements of registration. During the transition period, the individual IA shall be permitted to on-board new clients and collect fees in excess of the threshold limit as provided under Regulation 13 (g) of SEBI (Investment Advisers) Regulations, 2013.

title: Continue Advisory Activities as Individual IA if Non-Individual Registration is Not Granted
summary: Investment Advisers (IAs) must continue advisory activities as an individual IA while ensuring the applicable limits on the number of clients and fee collected, if non-individual registration is not granted.
trigger: If non-individual registration is not granted
required_action: Continue advisory activities as an individual IA while ensuring applicable limits on the number of clients and fee collected
evidence: Client Agreement Records, Fee Collection Records
verbatim_text: In case the aforesaid IA does not get registration as a non-individual IA, such IA shall continue the advisory activities as an Individual IA while ensuring the applicable limits on the number of clients and fee collected.

title: Maintain Arms-Length Relationship Between IA and RA Activities
summary: Ensure that investment advisory services are clearly segregated from research services.
trigger: Registration as an Investment Adviser or Research Analyst
required_action: Provide an undertaking stating the arms-length relationship and clear segregation of services.
evidence: Undertaking document signed by IA/RA
verbatim_text: Such IA/RA shall provide an undertaking stating that it shall maintain arms-length relationship between its activity as IA and RA and shall ensure that its investment advisory services and research services are clearly segregated from each other.

title: Maintain Arms-Length Relationship Between IA and Other Activities for Part-Time IAs
summary: Ensure clear segregation of investment advisory services from all other activities.
trigger: Registration as a Part-Time Investment Adviser
required_action: Provide an undertaking stating the arms-length relationship and clear segregation of services.
evidence: Undertaking document signed by part-time IA
verbatim_text: Part-time IA shall provide an undertaking stating that it shall maintain arms-length relationship between its activity as IA and other activities and shall ensure that its investment advisory services are clearly segregated from all its other activities at all stages of client engagement.

title: Provide Disclaimer for Other Services
summary: Clearly inform investors about the nature of other services provided.
trigger: Registration as a Part-Time Investment Adviser
required_action: Provide a disclaimer prominently in 10 font size or larger, attracting investor attention.
evidence: Disclaimers and invoices provided to clients
verbatim_text: Part-time IA shall provide disclaimer prominently (minimum 10 font size) and attracting the attention of the investor while providing their other service/raising invoice related to other business/service that the activity/invoice is related to services not under purview of SEBI and no complaint can be raised to SEBI for the services rendered therein.

title: Disclose Nature of Other Activities to Clients
summary: Investment Advisers (IAs) must disclose the nature of their other activities to clients and ensure there is no conflict of interest between IA activity and other business activities or employment.
trigger: Engaging in multiple activities
required_action: Disclose nature of other activities and ensure no conflict of interest
evidence: Disclosure document signed by IA and client
verbatim_text: The part-time IA shall disclose the nature of other activities to their clients and shall ensure that there is no conflict of interest between its IA activity and its other business activities or employment.

title: Eligibility for Registration as Part-time IA
summary: Investment Advisers must meet specific criteria to be eligible for registration as a part-time IA.
trigger: Applying for registration as a part-time IA
required_action: Meet eligibility criteria
evidence: Registration application with supporting documents
verbatim_text: For the purpose of providing additional clarity as to whether a person shall or shall not be considered eligible for registration as part-time IA, reference may be made to the following explanations/illustrations regarding other business activities or employment that a person shall or shall not engage in.

title: Eligibility Criteria - ICAI/ICSI/ICMAI Members
summary: Investment Advisers who are members of ICAI, ICSI, or ICMAI providing statutory services or insurance agents with IRDAI license are eligible for registration as part-time IA.
trigger: Applying for registration as a part-time IA
required_action: Be a member of ICAI, ICSI, or ICMAI providing statutory services or have IRDAI license
evidence: Membership certificate or IRDAI license
verbatim_text: A person shall be considered eligible for registration as part-time IA if it-(i) is a member of ICAI or ICSI or ICMAI providing their statutory services or an insurance agent having license from Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (‘IRDAI’).

title: Eligibility Criteria - Professional Individuals
summary: Investment Advisers who are professionals such as architects, lawyers, or doctors are eligible for registration as part-time IA.
trigger: Applying for registration as a part-time IA
required_action: Be a professional such as an architect, lawyer, or doctor
evidence: Professional certification or license
verbatim_text: A person shall be considered eligible for registration as part-time IA if it-(ii) is professional such as an architect, lawyer, doctor etc.

title: Eligibility Criteria - Educators
summary: Investment Advisers who are employed as professors or teachers or engaged in education business/activities may be eligible for registration as part-time IA, provided they do not engage in prohibited activities.
trigger: Applying for registration as a part-time IA
required_action: Be employed as a professor or teacher or engaged in education business/activities and not engage in prohibited activities
evidence: Employment contract or educational institution affiliation, along with proof of non-engagement in prohibited activities
verbatim_text: A person shall be considered eligible for registration as part-time IA if it-(iii) is employed as a professor or a teacher etc., or is engaged in education business or activity:

title: Prohibited Activities - Providing Advice on Securities
summary: Investment Advisers who provide advice/recommendations on securities without being registered with SEBI are not eligible for registration as part-time IA.
trigger: Applying for registration as a part-time IA and providing advice/recommendations on securities
required_action: Do not provide advice/recommendations on securities without SEBI registration
evidence: SEBI registration certificate or proof of compliance with SEBI regulations
verbatim_text: Provided that such person is not engaged in any of the two prohibited activities under Regulation 16A of Securities and Exchange Board of India (Intermediaries) Regulations, 2008 i.e.-(a) providing advice or any recommendation, directly or indirectly, in respect of or related to a security or securities, without being registered with or otherwise permitted by the SEBI to provide such advice or recommendation;

title: Prohibited Activities - Making Claims on Securities Performance
summary: Investment Advisers who make claims of returns or performance related to securities without SEBI permission are not eligible for registration as part-time IA.
trigger: Applying for registration as a part-time IA and making claims on securities performance
required_action: Do not make claims of returns or performance related to securities without SEBI permission
evidence: SEBI permission letter or proof of compliance with SEBI regulations
verbatim_text: (b) making any claim, of returns or performance expressly or impliedly, in respect of or related to a security or securities, without being permitted by the SEBI to make such a claim.

title: Eligibility Criteria - CA for Tax Planning/Tax Filing
summary: Investment Advisers who provide incidental advice on securities as an asset class to clients during tax planning/tax filing are not required to register as part-time IA.
trigger: Applying for registration as a part-time IA and providing incidental advice on securities
required_action: Provide incidental advice only, seek registration if providing security-specific advice
evidence: Documentation of incidental advice provided to clients during tax planning/tax filing
verbatim_text: If a CA for the purpose of tax planning/tax filing provides advice/recommendation on securities as an asset class to its client as an incidental advice to its primary activity, it is not required to get registered as a part-time IA.

title: Eligibility Criteria - CA Providing Security-Specific Advice
summary: Investment Advisers who provide security-specific advice to specific clients during tax planning/tax filing are required to register as part-time IA.
trigger: Applying for registration as a part-time IA and providing security-specific advice
required_action: Register as part-time IA if providing security-specific advice
evidence: Documentation of security-specific advice provided to clients during tax planning/tax filing, along with SEBI registration application
verbatim_text: However, if a CA is providing security-specific advice to a specific client, even though as part of tax planning/tax filing, it is required to seek registration as part-time IA.

title: Designation of Principal Officer for Partnership Firms
summary: In case of non-individual investment advisers being partnership firms, one partner must be designated as the principal officer.
trigger: Being a partnership firm and not an individual IA
required_action: Designate a principal officer
evidence: Designation document signed by partners
verbatim_text: Regulation 2(1)(s) of IA Regulations provides that in case of non-individual investment adviser being a partnership firm, one of the partners shall be designated as its principal officer.

title: Register as an Investment Adviser if No Partner Meets Qualification Requirements
summary: Apply for registration as a limited liability partnership or body corporate within the specified time if no partner meets the minimum qualification and certification requirements.
trigger: No partner of the registered investment adviser has the minimum qualification and certification requirements provided under the IA Regulations.
required_action: Apply for registration as a limited liability partnership or body corporate within the specified time.
evidence: Registration application form with supporting documents.
verbatim_text: In case no partner of the partnership firm registered as an investment adviser has minimum qualification and certification requirements provided under the IA Regulations, it shall apply for registration as an investment adviser in the form of a limited liability partnership or a body corporate within such time as may be specified by the SEBI.

title: Appoint an Independent Professional as Compliance Officer
summary: A non-individual investment adviser must appoint an independent professional who is a member of ICAI, ICSI, ICMAI or any other professional body specified by SEBI and holds relevant certification from NISM.
trigger: The IA is a non-individual entity.
required_action: Appoint an independent professional who meets the specified criteria as compliance officer.
evidence: Appointment letter and relevant certifications.
verbatim_text: In terms of Regulation 20 of the IA Regulations, a non-individual investment adviser may appoint an independent professional who is a member of ICAI or ICSI or ICMAI or member of any other professional body as may be specified by the SEBI, provided such a professional holds a relevant certification from NISM, as may be specified by the SEBI.

title: Submit Undertaking to IAASB/SEBI for Monitoring Compliance
summary: The principal officer of a non-individual investment adviser must submit an undertaking to IAASB/SEBI that they will monitor compliance with the Act, regulations, notifications, and guidelines issued by SEBI/IAASB.
trigger: The IA is a non-individual entity and has appointed an independent professional as compliance officer.
required_action: Submit an undertaking to IAASB/SEBI.
evidence: Undertaking document signed by the principal officer.
verbatim_text: In such cases, the principal officer shall submit an undertaking to IAASB/SEBI to the effect that principal officer shall be responsible for monitoring the compliance in respect of the requirements of the Act, regulations, notifications, guidelines issued by SEBI/IAASB.

title: Certifications Required for Compliance Officer
summary: A non-individual investment adviser must appoint a compliance officer who holds specific certifications from NISM.
trigger: The IA is a non-individual entity and has appointed an independent professional as compliance officer.
required_action: Ensure the compliance officer holds the required certifications.
evidence: Certification documents from NISM.
verbatim_text: A non-individual IA may appoint such an independent professional as compliance officer who holds certifications from NISM by passing the following certification examinations- • NISM-Series-X-A: Investment Adviser (Level 1) Certification Examination, • NISM-Series-X-B: Investment Adviser (Level 2) Certification Examination, • NISM-Series-X-C: Investment Adviser Certification (Renewal) Examination, and • NISM-Series-III A: Securities Intermediaries Compliance (Non-Fund) Certification Examination

title: Scope of Investment Advice
summary: Investment advice related to securities under SEBI’s purview falls within the IA Regulations, while financial planning services for products or services not under SEBI’s purview require specific disclosures and client declarations.
trigger: Providing investment advice or financial planning services to clients.
required_action: Ensure that the scope of activities complies with the IA Regulations, including making necessary disclosures for non-SEBI products/services.
evidence: Client declarations and disclosure documents.
verbatim_text: In terms of scope of the ‘investment advice’ under Regulation 2(1)(l) of the IA Regulations, Investment advice related to securities under purview of SEBI shall only fall under the purview of IA Regulations. It is however noted that IAs may also provide financial planning services to their clients and comprehensive financial planning may include the investment advice related to products or services not under the purview of SEBI. In this regard, the following is specified for IAs providing investment advice related to products or services not under the purview of SEBI to their clients- For the products and services not under the purview of SEBI, IA shall make disclosure to the client and take appropriate declaration and undertaking from the client that that such products/services and the services of IA in respect of such products/services do not come under regulatory purview of SEBI and that no recourse is available to them with SEBI for their grievances relat

title: Disclosure of Non-Regulated Products/Services
summary: IA must disclose that the products/services do not come under SEBI's regulatory purview and obtain a declaration from clients.
trigger: Onboarding new client or for existing clients as on January 8, 2025
required_action: Make disclosure and obtain appropriate declaration and undertaking
evidence: Client declaration and undertaking document
verbatim_text: IAs shall make the aforesaid disclosure and obtain appropriate declaration and undertaking while on-boarding new client.11 For existing clients as on January 8, 2025, IAs shall ensure compliance with these requirements latest by July 31, 2025.

title: Responsibility for AI Tools Usage and Disclosure
summary: IA must be responsible for the security, confidentiality, integrity of client data and disclose use of AI tools in providing investment advice.
trigger: Use of AI tools in IA services
required_action: Be solely responsible for security, confidentiality, integrity; disclose extent of use to clients
evidence: Client disclosure document and internal records of AI usage
verbatim_text: (a) In terms of Regulation 15(14) of the IA Regulations, an investment adviser who uses Artificial Intelligence tools, irrespective of the scale and scenario of adoption of such tools, for servicing its clients shall be solely responsible for the security, confidentiality, integrity of the client data, use of any other information or data to arrive at investment advice, investment advice based on output of Artificial Intelligence tools and compliance with any law for the time being in force. Further, in terms of Regulation 18(9) of the IA Regulations, an investment adviser shall disclose to the client the extent of use of Artificial Intelligence tools in providing investment advice.

title: Disclosure at Onboarding and Ongoing
summary: IA must provide disclosure on AI tool usage when entering into an agreement with clients and make additional disclosures as required.
trigger: Entering into an agreement or whenever required
required_action: Provide initial and ongoing disclosures about AI tool usage
evidence: Client disclosure document
verbatim_text: (b) Investment Adviser shall provide the disclosure of the extent of use of Artificial Intelligence tools by them in providing investment advice to their clients at the time of entering into the agreement and make such additional disclosure whenever required.

title: Maintenance of Records for Interactions with Clients
summary: IA must maintain records of all interactions, including prospective clients, from first interaction to completion of advisory services.
trigger: All client interactions
required_action: Maintain records in various forms and keep them for five years or longer if disputes arise
evidence: Client interaction records, call recordings, emails, SMS records, etc.
source_clause: Regulation 19(1) and Regulation 22A of the IA Regulations
verbatim_text: A. Regulation 19(1) of the IA Regulations provides that IA shall maintain records with respect to his activities as an IA. In this regard, it is clarified that: a) IA shall maintain records of interactions, with all clients including prospective clients (prior to onboarding), where any conversation related to advice has taken place inter alia, in the form of: i. Physical record written & signed by client, ii. Telephone recording, iii. Email from registered email id, iv. Record of SMS messages, v. Any other legally verifiable record. b) Such records shall begin with first interaction with the client and shall continue till the completion of advisory services to the client. B. Regulation 22A of the IA Regulations provides that IAs may provide implementation services to the advisory clients in securities market. In this regard, IAs providing implementation/execution services shall maintain call recording of every consent for implementation/execution obtained from the client if advice/execution is given through telephone call. All such communications shall have time stamped to maintain clear audit trail.

title: Retention Period for Records
summary: IA must retain records for five years, or longer if disputes arise.
trigger: Completion of advisory services to the client
required_action: Maintain records for a period of five years or until resolution of dispute
evidence: Client interaction records, call recordings, emails, SMS records, etc.

title: Conduct Annual Audit for Compliance
summary: Conduct an annual audit to ensure compliance with the IA Regulations and related circulars.
trigger: At the end of each financial year
required_action: Complete the annual compliance audit within six months from the end of each financial year, submit a report to IAASB/SEBI within one month, and maintain an annual certificate confirming compliance with client-level segregation requirements.
evidence: Annual compliance audit report, annual certificate from a member of ICAI/ICSI/ICMAI or an auditor, and submission records to IAASB/SEBI.
source_circular: SEBI Master Circular for Investment Advisers, HO/38/12/11(2)2026-MIRSD-POD/I/4300/2026, dated February 06, 2026
verbatim_text: As per regulation 19(3) of the IA Regulations, IA shall conduct annual audit in respect of compliance with SEBI (Investment Advisers) Regulations, 2013 and circulars issued thereunder. Annual compliance audit report shall specify each of the provisions of the IA Regulations and the circulars and guidelines issued thereunder upon which compliance is reported. An IA shall - (i) complete the annual compliance audit within six months from the end of each financial year and submit a compliance audit report to IAASB/SEBI within a period of one month from the date of the audit report. (ii) submit adverse findings of audit, if any, along with action taken thereof duly approved by the individual IA or management of non-individual IA to IAASB/SEBI within a period of one month from the date of the audit report but not later than October 31st of each year for the previous financial year; and (iii) maintain on record an annual certificate from a member of ICAI/ICSI/ ICMAI or from an auditor confirming compliance with client level segregation requirements. Such annual certificate shall be obtained within six months of the end of the financial year and form part of compliance audit, in terms of Regulation 19(3) of the IA Regulations.

title: Publish Audit Report on Website
summary: Publish the status of the annual compliance audit report and any adverse findings on the website.
trigger: After completing the annual audit
required_action: Publish the status of the compliance audit report and any adverse findings along with action taken thereof on the website, and provide the report to clients.
evidence: Website content showing published reports and actions taken for adverse findings.
source_circular: SEBI Master Circular for Investment Advisers, HO/38/12/11(2)2026-MIRSD-POD/I/4300/2026, dated February 06, 2026
verbatim_text: IA shall publish the status of the compliance audit report on its website and shall also publish the adverse findings of audit, if any, along with the action taken thereof on their website. IA shall provide the compliance audit report to its clients.

title: Risk Profiling and Suitability for Non-Individual Clients
summary: Conduct risk profiling and suitability analysis using the investment policy of non-individual clients.
trigger: Onboarding non-individual clients
required_action: Use the investment policy as approved by the board/management team for risk profiling and suitability analysis, and have discretion not to onboard if unable to do so.
evidence: Risk profiling reports and records of onboarding decisions.
source_circular: SEBI Master Circular for Investment Advisers, HO/38/12/11(2)2026-MIRSD-POD/I/4300/2026, dated February 06, 2026
verbatim_text: Regulations 16 and 17 of the IA Regulations mandate risk profiling and suitability for all categories of clients. In order to further enhance the risk profiling and encompass suitable factors in case of non-individual clients, IA shall use the investment policy as approved by board/management team of such non-individual clients for risk profiling and suitability analysis. The discretion to share the investment policy/relevant excerpts of the policy shall lie with the non-individual client. However, IA shall have discretion not to onboard non-individual clients if they are unable to do risk profiling of the non-individual client in the absence of investment policy.

title: Maintain Functional Website
summary: Maintain a functional website as per SEBI regulations.
trigger: At all times
required_action: Maintain a functional website containing details specified by SEBI.
evidence: Website content and records of updates made to the site.
source_circular: SEBI Master Circular for Investment Advisers, HO/38/12/11(2)2026-MIRSD-POD/I/4300/2026, dated February 06, 2026

required_action: Maintain a functional website with specified details

source_circular: SEBI Master Circular for Investment Advisers, HO/38/12/11(2)2026-MIRSD-POD/I/4300/2026, dated February 06, 2026
verbatim_text: Existing IAs, as on January 8, 2025, shall confirm the details of its website to IAASB latest by June 30, 2025.

title: Not provide free trial for any products/services
summary: Investment Advisers must not offer free trials of their services or products.
trigger: IA Regulations
required_action: Do not provide free trials for any products/services to prospective clients
evidence: Internal policies and procedures
source_circular: SEBI Master Circular for Investment Advisers, HO/38/12/11(2)2026-MIRSD-POD/I/4300/2026, dated February 06, 2026
verbatim_text: As per the IA Regulations, investment advice can be given after completing risk profiling of the client and ensuring suitability of the product. It has come to the notice that IAs are providing advice on free trial basis without considering risk profile of the client. Hence the IAs shall not provide free trial for any products/services to prospective clients.

title: Not accept part payments for any product/service
summary: Investment Advisers must not accept partial payment of fees in advance.
trigger: IA Regulations
required_action: Do not accept part payments (where some part of the fee is paid in advance) for any product/service
evidence: Internal policies and procedures
source_circular: SEBI Master Circular for Investment Advisers, HO/38/12/11(2)2026-MIRSD-POD/I/4300/2026, dated February 06, 2026
verbatim_text: As per the IA Regulations, investment advice can be given after completing risk profiling of the client and ensuring suitability of the product. It has come to the notice that IAs are providing advice on free trial basis without considering risk profile of the client. Hence the IAs shall not provide free trial for any products/services to prospective clients. Further, IAs shall not accept part payments (where some part of the fee is paid in advance) for any product/service.

title: Accept fees only via banking channels
summary: Investment Advisers must accept advisory fees strictly by account payee crossed cheques, demand draft or direct credit into their bank accounts through NEFT/RTGS/IMPS/UPI.
trigger: IA Regulations
required_action: Accept fees only via banking channels (account payee crossed cheques, demand draft or direct credit into their bank accounts through NEFT/RTGS/IMPS/UPI)
evidence: Bank statements and records of transactions
source_circular: SEBI Master Circular for Investment Advisers, HO/38/12/11(2)2026-MIRSD-POD/I/4300/2026, dated February 06, 2026
verbatim_text: It is observed that the IAs are receiving advisory fee in the form of cash deposit in their bank accounts or through payment gateways which does not provide proper audit trail of fees received from the clients. To bring transparency in dealing with the clients, IAs shall accept fees strictly by account payee crossed cheques / demand draft or by way of direct credit into their bank account through NEFT/ RTGS/IMPS/UPI. It is clarified that, IAs shall not accept cash deposits.

verbatim_text: Regulation 15(11) of the IA Regulations, IA shall obtain prior approval of SEBI in case of change in control. To streamline the process of providing approval to the proposed change in control of IA (hereinafter referred as IA or applicant), it has been decided as under:

title: Status of Past Applications

evidence: Report on past application status
