required_action: Do not share any login credentials for your trading, demat, or bank accounts.
evidence: No specific document required, but records of communication may be requested for verification.
verbatim_text: Do not share login credential and password of your trading, demat or bank accounts with the Investment Adviser.

title: Avoid disqualifications
summary: Investment Advisers must avoid certain disqualifying conditions as per Schedule II of SEBI (Intermediaries) Regulations, 2008.
trigger: Being a person in terms of Schedule II of SEBI (Intermediaries) Regulations, 2008
required_action: Ensure no criminal complaints, charge sheets, orders of restraint, prohibition or debarment, recovery proceedings, convictions for moral turpitude, winding up proceedings, declaration as insolvent, being found unsound mind by a court, categorized as a wilful defaulter, or declared as a fugitive economic offender.
evidence: Internal records and documentation of compliance with disqualification conditions.
verbatim_text: We bear integrity, honesty, ethical behaviour, reputation, fairness and character. We do not incur following disqualifications mentioned in Clause 3(b) of Schedule II of SEBI (Intermediaries) Regulations, 2008 i.e. (i) No criminal complaint or information under section 154 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (2 of 1974) has been filed against us by the Board and which is pending. (ii) No charge sheet has been filed against us by any enforcement agency in matters concerning economic offences and is pending. (iii) No order of restraint, prohibition or debarment has been passed against us by the Board or any other regulatory authority or enforcement agency in any matter concerning securities laws or financial markets and such order is in force. (iv) No recovery proceedings have been initiated by the Board against us and are pending. (v) No order of conviction has been passed against us by a court for any offence involving moral turpitude. (vi) No winding up proceedings have been initiated or an order for winding up has been passed against us. (vii) We have not been declared insolvent. (viii) We have not been found to be of unsound mind by a court of competent jurisdiction and no such finding is in force. (ix) We have not been categorized as a wilful defaulter. (x) We have not been declared a fugitive economic offender.

title: Avoid being declared unfit and proper person
summary: Investment Advisers must ensure they are not declared as 'not fit and proper persons' by SEBI.
trigger: Being a person in terms of Schedule II of SEBI (Intermediaries) Regulations, 2008
required_action: Ensure no declaration as 'not fit and proper persons' by an order of the Board.
evidence: Internal records and documentation of compliance with disqualification conditions.
verbatim_text: We have not been declared as not ‘fit and proper person’ by an order of the Board.

title: Avoid receiving notices for proceedings under SEBI regulations
summary: Investment Advisers must ensure they have not received any notice to show cause from SEBI or related sections during the last one year.
trigger: Being a person in terms of Schedule II of SEBI (Intermediaries) Regulations, 2008
required_action: Ensure no notice to show cause has been issued for proceedings under SEBI(Intermediaries) Regulations, 2008 or under section 11(4) or section 11B of the SEBI Act during last one year.
evidence: Internal records and documentation of compliance with disqualification conditions.
verbatim_text: No notice to show cause has been issued for proceedings under SEBI(Intermediaries) Regulations, 2008 or under section 11(4) or section 11B of the SEBI Act during last one year against us.

title: Maintain stable board composition
summary: Investment Advisers must ensure no change in their Board of Directors until prior approval is granted.
trigger: Granting of prior approval by SEBI for a proposed change in management.
required_action: Ensure there will not be any change in the Board of Directors of incumbent, till the time prior approval is granted.
evidence: Internal records and documentation of compliance with board stability conditions.
verbatim_text: We hereby undertake that there will not be any change in the Board of Directors of incumbent, till the time prior approval is granted.

title: Notify existing clients about management changes
summary: Investment Advisers must inform all existing investors/clients about proposed changes in management before effecting them.
trigger: Granting of prior approval by SEBI for a proposed change in management.
required_action: Inform all the existing investors/ clients about the proposed change prior to effecting the same, in order to enable them to take informed decision regarding their continuance or otherwise with the new management.
evidence: Internal records and documentation of client notifications.
verbatim_text: We hereby undertake that pursuant to grant of prior approval by SEBI, the incumbent shall inform all the existing investors/ clients about the proposed change prior to effecting the same, in order to enable them to take informed decision regarding their continuance or otherwise with the new management. The said information is true to our knowledge.

title: Establish an outsourcing policy
summary: Develop a policy covering activities that can be outsourced, approval authorities, and third-party selection.
trigger: When engaging in any form of outsourcing activity
required_action: Create an outsourcing policy document
evidence: Outsourcing policy document
verbatim_text: The policy shall cover activities or the nature of activities that can be outsourced, the authorities who can approve outsourcing of such activities, and the selection of third party to whom it can be outsourced.

title: Regularly review the outsourcing policy
summary: Review the outsourcing policy regularly in response to changes in the business environment.
trigger: In response to changing business conditions
required_action: Conduct a regular review of the outsourcing policy
evidence: Minutes of the board meeting or review report
verbatim_text: The Board shall mandate a regular review of outsourcing policy for such activities in the wake of changing business environment. It shall also have overall responsibility for ensuring that all ongoing outsourcing decisions taken by the intermediary and the activities undertaken by the third-party, are in keeping with its outsourcing policy.

title: Establish a risk management programme for outsourced activities
summary: Develop a comprehensive risk management programme to address risks associated with outsourced activities.
trigger: When engaging in any form of outsourcing activity
required_action: Implement a risk management programme for all outsourced activities
evidence: Risk management programme documentation
verbatim_text: An intermediary shall make an assessment of outsourcing risk which depends on several factors, including the scope and materiality of the outsourced activity, etc. While there shall not be any prohibition on a group entity / associate of the intermediary to act as the third party, systems shall be put in place to have an arm’s length distance between the intermediary and the third party in terms of infrastructure, manpower, decision-making, record keeping, etc. for avoidance of potential conflict of interests.

title: Preserve Outsourcing Records Centrally
summary: Investment Advisers must preserve records of all outsourced activities centrally for review by the Board or senior management.
trigger: All activities outsourced to an unrelated party
required_action: Preserve records centrally and regularly update them.
evidence: Centralized record-keeping system with updated records.
verbatim_text: The records relating to all activities outsourced shall be preserved centrally so that the same is readily accessible for review by the Board of the intermediary and / or its senior management, as and when needed. Such records shall be regularly updated and may also form part of the corporate governance review by the management of the intermediary.

title: Regular Audits of Outsourcing Arrangements
summary: Investment Advisers must conduct regular reviews and audits of outsourcing policies, risk management systems, and regulatory requirements.
trigger: Wherever felt necessary by the Board
required_action: Conduct internal or external audits regularly.
evidence: Audit reports and documentation of reviews conducted.
verbatim_text: Regular reviews by internal or external auditors of the outsourcing policies, risk management system and requirements of the regulator shall be mandated by the Board wherever felt necessary. The intermediary shall review the financial and operational capabilities of the third party in order to assess its ability to continue to meet its outsourcing obligations.

title: Ensure Outsourcing Does Not Diminish Obligations
summary: Investment Advisers must ensure that outsourcing does not diminish their ability to fulfill customer and regulatory obligations.
trigger: Outsourcing arrangements are made
required_action: Ensure that outsourcing does not diminish the ability to fulfill obligations.
evidence: Documentation showing compliance with this obligation.
verbatim_text: The intermediary shall ensure that outsourcing arrangements neither diminish its ability to fulfill its obligations to customers and regulators, nor impede effective supervision by the regulators.

title: Full Liability for Outsourced Activities
summary: Investment Advisers must be fully liable for activities outsourced as if they were provided in-house.
trigger: Outsourcing arrangements are made
required_action: Be fully liable and accountable for the activities being outsourced.
evidence: Documentation showing full liability for outsourced activities.
verbatim_text: The intermediary shall be fully liable and accountable for the activities that are being outsourced to the same extent as if the service were provided in-house.

title: Protect Investor Rights Against Outsourcing
summary: Investment Advisers must ensure that outsourcing does not affect investors' rights and be liable for any loss incurred by them.
trigger: Outsourcing arrangements are made
required_action: Ensure investor rights are protected and be liable for losses due to third-party failure.
evidence: Documentation showing compliance with this obligation.
verbatim_text: Outsourcing arrangements shall not affect the rights of an investor or client in any manner. The intermediary shall be liable to the investors for the loss incurred by them due to the failure of the third party and also be responsible for redressal of the grievances received from investors arising out of activities rendered by the third party.

title: Access to Outsourced Premises/Data
summary: Investment Advisers must have access to facilities, premises, and data used in outsourced activities.
trigger: Outsourcing arrangements are made
required_action: Ensure right of access to the service provider's facilities, premises, and data.
evidence: Documentation showing compliance with this obligation.
verbatim_text: The facilities / premises / data that are involved in carrying out the outsourced activity by the service provider shall be deemed to be those of the registered intermediary. The intermediary itself and Regulator or the persons authorized by it shall have the right to access the same at any point of time.

title: Ensure Supervision/Inspection Not Impaired
summary: Investment Advisers must ensure that outsourcing does not impair SEBI/SRO's ability to supervise and inspect.
trigger: Outsourcing arrangements are made
required_action: Ensure supervision/inspection is not impaired by outsourcing.
evidence: Documentation showing compliance with this obligation.
verbatim_text: Outsourcing arrangements shall not impair the ability of SEBI/SRO or auditors to exercise its regulatory responsibilities such as supervision/inspection of the intermediary.

title: Conduct Due Diligence in Selecting Third Party
summary: Investment Advisers must conduct due diligence to select a third party capable of performing outsourced activities effectively.
trigger: Outsourcing arrangements are made
required_action: Conduct appropriate due diligence in selecting the third party and monitoring its performance.
evidence: Documentation showing due diligence conducted.
verbatim_text: The intermediary shall conduct appropriate due diligence in selecting the third party and in monitoring of its performance.

title: Assess Third Party's Resources and Capabilities
summary: Investment Advisers must assess a third party’s resources, financial soundness, and ability to perform outsourced activities within timelines.
trigger: Outsourcing arrangements are made
required_action: Assess the third party's resources, capabilities, financial soundness, and ability to meet timelines.
evidence: Documentation showing assessment of the third party’s resources and capabilities.
verbatim_text: The due diligence undertaken by an intermediary shall include assessment of: third party’s resources and capabilities, including financial soundness, to perform the outsourcing work within the timelines fixed;

title: Assess Compatibility with Intermediary's Requirements
summary: Investment Advisers must assess compatibility of third party’s practices and systems with their requirements and objectives.
trigger: Outsourcing arrangements are made
required_action: Assess the compatibility of the third party's practices and systems with intermediary's requirements and objectives.
evidence: Documentation showing assessment of compatibility.
verbatim_text: The due diligence undertaken by an intermediary shall include assessment of: compatibility of the practices and systems of the third party with the intermediary’s requirements and objectives;

title: Assess Market Feedback on Third Party's Reputation
summary: Investment Advisers must assess market feedback on a third party's business reputation and track record.
trigger: Outsourcing arrangements are made
required_action: Assess the market feedback of the prospective third party’s business reputation and track record.
evidence: Documentation showing assessment of market feedback.
verbatim_text: The due diligence undertaken by an intermediary shall include assessment of: market feedback of the prospective third party’s business reputation and track record of their services rendered in the past;

title: Assess Level of Concentration with Third Party
summary: Investment Advisers must assess the level of concentration of outsourced arrangements with a single third party.
trigger: Outsourcing arrangements are made
required_action: Assess the level of concentration of outsourced arrangements with a single third party.
evidence: Documentation showing assessment of concentration levels.
verbatim_text: The due diligence undertaken by an intermediary shall include assessment of: level of concentration of the outsourced arrangements with a single third party;

title: Assess Foreign Country Environment
summary: Investment Advisers must assess the environment of the foreign country where the third party is located.
trigger: Outsourcing arrangements are made with a foreign third party
required_action: Assess the environment of the foreign country where the third party is located.
evidence: Documentation showing assessment of the foreign country's environment.
verbatim_text: The due diligence undertaken by an intermediary shall include assessment of: the environment of the foreign country

title: Establish Written Contracts for Outsourcing Arrangements
summary: Investment Advisers must establish written contracts for all outsourcing arrangements.
trigger: Outsourcing of activities to third parties
required_action: Governing by a clearly defined and legally binding written contract
evidence: Copies of the contracts
verbatim_text: Outsourcing arrangements shall be governed by a clearly defined and legally binding written contract between the intermediary and each of the third parties, the nature and detail of which shall be appropriate to the materiality of the outsourced activity in relation to the ongoing business of the intermediary.

title: Define Activities and Performance Levels in Contracts
summary: Investment Advisers must clearly define what activities are going to be outsourced, including appropriate service and performance levels.
trigger: Outsourcing of activities to third parties
required_action: Clearly defining the activities and performance levels in the contract
evidence: Copies of the contracts
verbatim_text: 5.2.1. clearly defines what activities are going to be outsourced, including appropriate service and performance levels;

title: Define Rights, Obligations, and Responsibilities in Contracts
summary: Investment Advisers must provide for mutual rights, obligations, and responsibilities of the intermediary and the third party.
trigger: Outsourcing of activities to third parties
required_action: Providing for mutual rights, obligations, and responsibilities in the contract
evidence: Copies of the contracts
verbatim_text: 5.2.2. provides for mutual rights, obligations and responsibilities of the intermediary and the third party, including indemnity by the parties;

title: Define Liability for Unsatisfactory Performance in Contracts

trigger: Outsourcing of activities to third parties
required_action: Providing for the liability in the contract
evidence: Copies of the contracts
verbatim_text: 5.2.3. provides for the liability of the third party to the intermediary for unsatisfactory performance/other breach of the contract

title: Ensure Continuous Monitoring and Assessment in Contracts
summary: Investment Advisers must ensure continuous monitoring and assessment by the intermediary to maintain control over the outsourcing.
trigger: Outsourcing of activities to third parties
required_action: Continuous monitoring and assessment by the intermediary
evidence: Monitoring reports, records of assessments
verbatim_text: 5.2.4. provides for the continuous monitoring and assessment by the intermediary of the third party so that any necessary corrective measures can be taken up immediately, i.e., the contract shall enable the intermediary to retain an appropriate level of control over the outsourcing and the right to intervene with appropriate measures to meet legal and regulatory obligations;

title: Include Conditions for Sub-Contracting in Contracts
summary: Investment Advisers must include conditions of sub-contracting by the third party.
trigger: Outsourcing of activities to third parties
required_action: Including conditions for sub-contracting in the contract
evidence: Copies of the contracts
verbatim_text: 5.2.5. includes, where necessary, conditions of sub-contracting by the third-party, i.e. the contract shall enable intermediary to maintain a similar control over the risks when a third party outsources to further third parties as in the original direct outsourcing;

title: Include Confidentiality Clauses in Contracts
summary: Investment Advisers must include unambiguous confidentiality clauses in contracts.
trigger: Outsourcing of activities to third parties
required_action: Including unambiguous confidentiality clauses in the contract
evidence: Copies of the contracts
verbatim_text: 5.2.6. has unambiguous confidentiality clauses to ensure protection of proprietary and customer data during the tenure of the contract and also after the expiry of the contract;

title: Include IT Security Clauses in Contracts
summary: Investment Advisers must include clauses related to IT security, contingency plans, insurance cover, business continuity and disaster recovery plans.
trigger: Outsourcing of activities to third parties
required_action: Including clauses related to IT security, contingency plans, insurance cover, business continuity and disaster recovery plans in the contract
evidence: Copies of the contracts
verbatim_text: 5.2.7. specifies the responsibilities of the third party with respect to the IT security and contingency plans, insurance cover, business continuity and disaster recovery plans, force majeure clause, etc.

title: Preserve Documents and Data in Contracts
summary: Investment Advisers must provide for the preservation of documents and data by third parties.
trigger: Outsourcing of activities to third parties
required_action: Providing for the preservation of documents and data in the contract
evidence: Copies of the contracts
verbatim_text: 5.2.8. provides for preservation of the documents and data by third party;

title: Include Termination Provisions in Contracts
summary: Investment Advisers must include provisions related to termination, rights, transfer of information and exit strategies.
trigger: Outsourcing of activities to third parties
required_action: Including provisions related to termination, rights, transfer of information and exit strategies in the contract
evidence: Copies of the contracts
verbatim_text: 5.2.10. provides for termination of the contract, termination rights, transfer of information and exit strategies;

title: Address Country Risks in Contracts
summary: Investment Advisers must address country risks and potential obstacles in exercising oversight and management of the arrangements.
trigger: Outsourcing to foreign third parties
required_action: Addressing country risks and potential obstacles in the contract
evidence: Copies of the contracts
verbatim_text: 5.2.11. addresses additional issues arising from country risks and potential obstacles in exercising oversight and management of the arrangements when intermediary outsources its activities to foreign third party. For example, the contract shall i

title: Inclusion of Choice-of-Law Provisions and Jurisdictional Covenants in Contracts
summary: Include choice-of-law provisions, agreement covenants, and jurisdictional covenants that provide for adjudication of disputes under the laws of a specific jurisdiction.
trigger: When intermediary outsources activities to foreign third parties
required_action: Include choice-of-law provisions, agreement covenants, and jurisdictional covenants in contracts with third parties.
evidence: Contractual agreements with third parties showing inclusion of required provisions.
verbatim_text: For example, the contract shall include choice-of-law provisions and agreement covenants and jurisdictional covenants that provide for adjudication of disputes between the parties under the laws of a specific jurisdiction;

title: Ensuring Outsourcing Does Not Impede Regulatory Compliance
summary: Ensure outsourcing does not prevent or impede meeting regulatory obligations and allow regulators to exercise their powers.
trigger: When intermediary outsources activities to third parties
required_action: Ensure that outsourcing arrangements do not hinder the ability to meet regulatory obligations and allow for regulator oversight.
evidence: Documentation showing compliance with regulatory requirements and access agreements with regulators.
verbatim_text: 5.2.12. neither prevents nor impedes the intermediary from meeting its respective regulatory obligations, nor the regulator from exercising its regulatory powers;

title: Granting Access to Books and Records for Regulatory Oversight
summary: Provide access to books, records, and information relevant to outsourced activities.
trigger: When intermediary outsources activities to third parties
required_action: Ensure that regulators or authorized persons can inspect and access all necessary documents and information related to the outsourced activity.
evidence: Access agreements with third parties and regulators, documentation of inspections.
verbatim_text: 5.2.13. provides for the intermediary and/or the regulator or the persons authorized by it to have the ability to inspect, access all books, records and information relevant to the outsourced activity with the third party.

title: Establishment of Contingency Plans for Outsourcing Arrangements
summary: Develop and maintain contingency plans, including disaster recovery plans, for each outsourcing arrangement.
trigger: When intermediary outsources activities to third parties
required_action: Create separate contingency plans for each outsourcing arrangement and ensure they are robust and tested regularly.
evidence: Documentation of developed contingency plans, test results, and regular reviews.
verbatim_text: The intermediary and its third parties shall establish and maintain contingency plans, including a plan for disaster recovery and periodic testing of backup facilities. Specific contingency plans shall be separately developed for each outsourcing arrangement, as is done in individual business lines. An intermediary shall take appropriate steps to assess and address the potential consequence of a business disruption or other problems at the third party level. Notably, it shall consider contingency plans at the third party; co-ordination of contingency plans at both the intermediary and the third party; and contingency plans of the intermediary in the event of non-performance by the third party. To ensure business continuity, robust information technology security is a necessity. A breakdown in the IT capacity may impair the ability of the intermediary to fulfill its obligations to other market participants/clients/regulators and could undermine the privacy interests of its customers, harm the intermediary’s reputation, and may ultimately impact on its overall operational risk profile. Intermediaries shall, therefore, seek to ensure that third party maintains appropriate IT security and robust disaster recovery capabilities. Periodic tests of the critical security procedures and systems and review of the backup facilities shall be undertaken by the intermediary to confirm the adequacy of the third party’s systems.

title: Protection of Confidential Information from Third Parties
summary: Ensure that confidential information is protected and not misused or misappropriated by third parties.
trigger: When intermediary outsources activities to third parties
required_action: Take appropriate steps to protect proprietary and confidential customer information from misuse or misappropriation, limit access to data on a need-to-know basis, and ensure adequate checks and balances.
evidence: Documentation of policies and procedures for protecting confidential information, agreements with third parties regarding data handling, and records of employee training.
verbatim_text: The intermediary shall take appropriate steps to require that third parties protect confidential information of both the intermediary and its customers from intentional or inadvertent disclosure to unauthorised persons. An intermediary that engages in outsourcing is expected to take appropriate steps to protect its proprietary and confidential customer information and ensure that it is not misused or misappropriated. The intermediary shall prevail upon the third party to ensure that the employees of the third party have limited access to the data handled and only on a ‘need to know’ basis and the third party shall have adequate checks and balances to ensure the same.
